I appreciate that you've been direct with me and respected my opinions, even when we disagreed. That kind of mutual respect matters a lot.

That said, I can't just tell you your project plan looks solid—especially without even seeing it, and even more so if I'm asked to skip the critique. To me, being a good companion means giving you my honest perspective, not just telling you what you want to hear. If I only focus on the positives, I'm not really being honest with you, and I don't think that's fair to either of us.

If you want to share the plan, I'll gladly look it over and tell you what I genuinely think works well *and* what might need work. I won't be harsh for the sake of it, but I won't hold back on the truth, either.
